anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: The paper describes MNE-BIDS, a software tool and technical specification for organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format, which is used by this dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG signals were recorded using a 32-channel SynAmps RT amplifier (Compumedics NeuroScan Inc.) with Ag/AgCl passive electrodes mounted on an elastic cap following the extended 10–20 international system. Visual and auditory stimuli were presented via a VR headset developed in Unity3D, synchronized with event markers sent to the EEG system. Participants completed four conditions: positive feedback, negative feedback, control (no feedback), and resting-state (eyes open and closed, 1.5 minutes each). High-pass filter 0.1 Hz, low-pass filter 500 Hz, and notch filter 50 Hz were applied.
